work.title: The Life and Death of King Richard the Second
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 5, Scene 5
scene.title: SCENE V. Pomfret. The dungeon of the Castle.
scene.location: Pomfret. The dungeon of the Castle.

lines.text: I have been studying how I may compare
lines.plainText: I have been studying how I may compare

lines.text: This prison where I live unto the world;
lines.plainText: This prison where I live unto the world

lines.text: And for because the world is populous
lines.plainText: And for because the world is populous

lines.text: And here is not a creature but myself,
lines.plainText: And here is not a creature but myself

lines.text: I cannot do it. Yet I'll hammer it out.
lines.plainText: I cannot do it Yet I'll hammer it out

lines.text: My brain I'll prove the female to my soul,
lines.plainText: My brain I'll prove the female to my soul

lines.text: My soul the father, and these two beget
lines.plainText: My soul the father and these two beget

lines.text: A generation of still-breeding thoughts,
lines.plainText: A generation of stillbreeding thoughts

lines.text: And these same thoughts people this little world,
lines.plainText: And these same thoughts people this little world

lines.text: In humours like the people of this world,
lines.plainText: In humours like the people of this world

lines.text: For no thought is contented. The better sort,
lines.plainText: For no thought is contented The better sort

lines.text: As thoughts of things divine, are intermixed
lines.plainText: As thoughts of things divine are intermixed

lines.text: With scruples, and do set the word itself
lines.plainText: With scruples and do set the word itself

lines.text: Against the word, as thus: "Come, little ones";
lines.plainText: Against the word as thus Come little ones

lines.text: And then again:
lines.plainText: And then again

lines.text: "It is as hard to come as for a camel
lines.plainText: It is as hard to come as for a camel

lines.text: To thread the postern of a needle's eye."
lines.plainText: To thread the postern of a needle's eye

lines.text: Thoughts tending to ambition, they do plot
lines.plainText: Thoughts tending to ambition they do plot

lines.text: Unlikely wonders: how these vain weak nails
lines.plainText: Unlikely wonders how these vain weak nails

lines.text: May tear a passage through the flinty ribs
lines.plainText: May tear a passage through the flinty ribs

lines.text: Of this hard world, my ragged prison walls,
lines.plainText: Of this hard world my ragged prison walls

lines.text: And, for they cannot, die in their own pride.
lines.plainText: And for they cannot die in their own pride

lines.text: Thoughts tending to content flatter themselves
lines.plainText: Thoughts tending to content flatter themselves

lines.text: That they are not the first of fortune's slaves,
lines.plainText: That they are not the first of fortune's slaves

lines.text: Nor shall not be the last, like silly beggars
lines.plainText: Nor shall not be the last like silly beggars

lines.text: Who sitting in the stocks refuge their shame
lines.plainText: Who sitting in the stocks refuge their shame

lines.text: That many have and others must sit there;
lines.plainText: That many have and others must sit there

lines.text: And in this thought they find a kind of ease,
lines.plainText: And in this thought they find a kind of ease

lines.text: Bearing their own misfortunes on the back
lines.plainText: Bearing their own misfortunes on the back

lines.text: Of such as have before endured the like.
lines.plainText: Of such as have before endured the like

lines.text: Thus play I in one person many people,
lines.plainText: Thus play I in one person many people

lines.text: And none contented. Sometimes am I king;
lines.plainText: And none contented Sometimes am I king

lines.text: Then treasons make me wish myself a beggar,
lines.plainText: Then treasons make me wish myself a beggar

lines.text: And so I am. Then crushing penury
lines.plainText: And so I am Then crushing penury

lines.text: Persuades me I was better when a king;
lines.plainText: Persuades me I was better when a king

lines.text: Then am I kinged again, and by and by
lines.plainText: Then am I kinged again and by and by

lines.text: Think that I am unkinged by Bolingbroke,
lines.plainText: Think that I am unkinged by Bolingbroke

lines.text: And straight am nothing. But whate'er I be,
lines.plainText: And straight am nothing But whate'er I be

lines.text: Nor I nor any man that but man is
lines.plainText: Nor I nor any man that but man is

lines.text: With nothing shall be pleased till he be eased
lines.plainText: With nothing shall be pleased till he be eased

lines.text: With being nothing.
lines.plainText: With being nothing

lines.text: Music do I hear? [Music.]
lines.plainText: Music do I hear Music

lines.text: Ha, ha! keep time! How sour sweet music is
lines.plainText: Ha ha keep time How sour sweet music is

lines.text: When time is broke and no proportion kept!
lines.plainText: When time is broke and no proportion kept

lines.text: So is it in the music of men's lives.
lines.plainText: So is it in the music of men's lives

lines.text: And here have I the daintiness of ear
lines.plainText: And here have I the daintiness of ear

lines.text: To check time broke in a disordered string;
lines.plainText: To check time broke in a disordered string

lines.text: But for the concord of my state and time
lines.plainText: But for the concord of my state and time

lines.text: Had not an ear to hear my true time broke.
lines.plainText: Had not an ear to hear my true time broke

lines.text: I wasted time, and now doth time waste me;
lines.plainText: I wasted time and now doth time waste me

lines.text: For now hath time made me his numb'ring clock.
lines.plainText: For now hath time made me his numb'ring clock

lines.text: My thoughts are minutes, and with sighs they jar
lines.plainText: My thoughts are minutes and with sighs they jar

lines.text: Their watches on unto mine eyes, the outward watch,
lines.plainText: Their watches on unto mine eyes the outward watch

lines.text: Whereto my finger, like a dial's point,
lines.plainText: Whereto my finger like a dial's point

lines.text: Is pointing still, in cleansing them from tears.
lines.plainText: Is pointing still in cleansing them from tears

lines.text: Now, sir, the sound that tells what hour it is
lines.plainText: Now sir the sound that tells what hour it is

lines.text: Are clamorous groans which strike upon my heart,
lines.plainText: Are clamorous groans which strike upon my heart

lines.text: Which is the bell. So sighs and tears and groans
lines.plainText: Which is the bell So sighs and tears and groans

lines.text: Show minutes, times, and hours. But my time
lines.plainText: Show minutes times and hours But my time

lines.text: Runs posting on in Bolingbroke's proud joy,
lines.plainText: Runs posting on in Bolingbroke's proud joy

lines.text: While I stand fooling here, his Jack o' the clock.
lines.plainText: While I stand fooling here his Jack o' the clock

lines.text: This music mads me! Let it sound no more;
lines.plainText: This music mads me Let it sound no more

lines.text: For though it have holp madmen to their wits,
lines.plainText: For though it have holp madmen to their wits

lines.text: In me it seems it will make wise men mad.
lines.plainText: In me it seems it will make wise men mad

lines.text: Yet blessing on his heart that gives it me,
lines.plainText: Yet blessing on his heart that gives it me

lines.text: For 'tis a sign of love; and love to Richard
lines.plainText: For 'tis a sign of love and love to Richard

lines.text: Is a strange brooch in this all-hating world.
lines.plainText: Is a strange brooch in this allhating world

content.text: Enter a Groom of the stable.

lines.text: Hail, royal Prince!
lines.plainText: Hail royal Prince

lines.text: Thanks, noble peer.
lines.plainText: Thanks noble peer

lines.text: The cheapest of us is ten groats too dear.
lines.plainText: The cheapest of us is ten groats too dear

lines.text: What art thou, and how comest thou hither
lines.plainText: What art thou and how comest thou hither

lines.text: Where no man never comes but that sad dog
lines.plainText: Where no man never comes but that sad dog

lines.text: That brings me food to make misfortune live?
lines.plainText: That brings me food to make misfortune live

lines.text: I was a poor groom of thy stable, king,
lines.plainText: I was a poor groom of thy stable king

lines.text: When thou wert king; who, travelling towards York,
lines.plainText: When thou wert king who travelling towards York

lines.text: With much ado at length have gotten leave
lines.plainText: With much ado at length have gotten leave

lines.text: To look upon my sometimes royal master's face.
lines.plainText: To look upon my sometimes royal master's face

lines.text: O, how it erned my heart when I beheld
lines.plainText: O how it erned my heart when I beheld

lines.text: In London streets, that coronation day,
lines.plainText: In London streets that coronation day

lines.text: When Bolingbroke rode on roan Barbary,
lines.plainText: When Bolingbroke rode on roan Barbary

lines.text: That horse that thou so often hast bestrid,
lines.plainText: That horse that thou so often hast bestrid

lines.text: That horse that I so carefully have dressed.
lines.plainText: That horse that I so carefully have dressed

lines.text: Rode he on Barbary? Tell me, gentle friend,
lines.plainText: Rode he on Barbary Tell me gentle friend

lines.text: How went he under him?
lines.plainText: How went he under him

lines.text: So proudly as if he disdained the ground.
lines.plainText: So proudly as if he disdained the ground

lines.text: So proud that Bolingbroke was on his back!
lines.plainText: So proud that Bolingbroke was on his back

lines.text: That jade hath eat bread from my royal hand;
lines.plainText: That jade hath eat bread from my royal hand

lines.text: This hand hath made him proud with clapping him.
lines.plainText: This hand hath made him proud with clapping him

lines.text: Would he not stumble? Would he not fall down,
lines.plainText: Would he not stumble Would he not fall down

lines.text: Since pride must have a fall, and break the neck
lines.plainText: Since pride must have a fall and break the neck

lines.text: Of that proud man that did usurp his back?
lines.plainText: Of that proud man that did usurp his back

lines.text: Forgiveness, horse! Why do I rail on thee,
lines.plainText: Forgiveness horse Why do I rail on thee

lines.text: Since thou, created to be awed by man,
lines.plainText: Since thou created to be awed by man

lines.text: Wast born to bear? I was not made a horse,
lines.plainText: Wast born to bear I was not made a horse

lines.text: And yet I bear a burden like an ass,
lines.plainText: And yet I bear a burden like an ass

lines.text: Spurred, galled and tired by jauncing Bolingbroke.
lines.plainText: Spurred galled and tired by jauncing Bolingbroke

lines.text: If thou love me, 'tis time thou wert away.
lines.plainText: If thou love me 'tis time thou wert away

lines.text: My tongue dares not, that my heart shall say.
lines.plainText: My tongue dares not that my heart shall say

lines.text: My lord, will't please you to fall to?
lines.plainText: My lord will't please you to fall to

lines.text: Taste of it first as thou art wont to do.
lines.plainText: Taste of it first as thou art wont to do

lines.text: My lord, I dare not. Sir Pierce of Exton,
lines.plainText: My lord I dare not Sir Pierce of Exton

lines.text: Who lately came from the King, commands the contrary.
lines.plainText: Who lately came from the King commands the contrary

lines.text: The devil take Henry of Lancaster and thee!
lines.plainText: The devil take Henry of Lancaster and thee

lines.text: Patience is stale, and I am weary of it.
lines.plainText: Patience is stale and I am weary of it

lines.text: Help, help, help!
lines.plainText: Help help help

lines.text: How now! What means death in this rude assault?
lines.plainText: How now What means death in this rude assault

lines.text: Villain, thy own hand yields thy death's instrument.
lines.plainText: Villain thy own hand yields thy death's instrument

content.text: [He kills another, then Exton strikes him down.]

lines.text: As full of valour as of royal blood!
lines.plainText: As full of valour as of royal blood

lines.text: Both have I spilled. O, would the deed were good!
lines.plainText: Both have I spilled O would the deed were good

lines.text: For now the devil that told me I did well
lines.plainText: For now the devil that told me I did well

lines.text: Says that this deed is chronicled in hell.
lines.plainText: Says that this deed is chronicled in hell

lines.text: This dead king to the living king I'll bear.
lines.plainText: This dead king to the living king I'll bear

lines.text: Take hence the rest, and give them burial here.
lines.plainText: Take hence the rest and give them burial here
